0.description: Identifier of the entry in `verticalBoundaryDefinitions` that establishes this boundary, when `state` indicates a source definition exists.
Identifier of the derived boundary geometry (e.g. an upper or lower surface) realising this boundary, when `state` is derived.
The state of this boundary: undefined, not applicable, unconstrained, defined but unresolved, defined, or derived. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `vertical-boundary-state:und`).

properties.description: How the feature's spatial representation currently stands: 2D footprint only, 2.5D (footprint plus reference surface), height-described, jurisdictionally bounded, or derived 3D. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `representation-status:2d`).

Which geometry is legally authoritative for the feature: the 2D footprint, an observed surface, or geometry derived from a legal description. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `geometry-legal-status:a2d`).
The number of ordinates carried by the feature's coordinates.

What a third coordinate ordinate, if present, means: absent, a contextual geometry height, a reference-surface height, or a derived-boundary height. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `coordinate-z-role:absent`).
The overall legal or source state of the vertical extent. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `vertical-extent-status:ud`).
Identifier of the supporting source document, where the extent's status (e.g. a positively established unconstrained extent) is itself sourced.
Whether coordinate boundaries or geometry can be calculated from the information currently available. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `computability-status:nc`).

The source definitions (relative offset, absolute datum value, or jurisdictional rule) that establish or describe a vertical boundary. Kept separate from any computed/derived geometry — see `derivedGeometry`.
Local identifier for this definition, referenced by `verticalExtent.lowerBoundary.definitionRef` / `upperBoundary.definitionRef` and by `derivedGeometry.inputDefinitionRefs`.

The kind of source definition: relative height description, absolute height description, jurisdictional boundary rule, or geometry boundary reference. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `vertical-definition-type:rel`).
Whether this definition establishes an upper or lower limit. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `vertical-limit-role:ll`).
How `value` is expressed: as an offset from a reference, or as an absolute height/depth. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `vertical-value-type:off`).
The numeric height, depth, or offset value.
The direction in which `value` is expressed (above or below the reference), where relevant. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `vertical-direction:blw`).
The surface, level, object, plane or datum that `value` is relative to. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `height-reference:gl`).
Human-readable description or verbatim source wording for this boundary definition.
The comparison implied by an absolute value, e.g. `lessThanOrEqual` or `greaterThanOrEqual`.
Whether this definition has been resolved into a computable absolute value, e.g. `requiresReferenceSurface`, `absoluteLimitAvailable`, or `resolved`.
Identifier of the supporting source document for this definition.
Identifier of the PROV activity that extracted or derived this definition.

Reference surfaces (terrain, ground, floor, or other surface) that provide vertical context for the feature. A reference surface supports analysis or visualisation; it is not by itself a legal vertical boundary.
Local identifier for this reference surface, referenced by `derivedGeometry.inputSurfaceRefs`.
What the surface represents, e.g. ground level. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `height-reference:gl`).
The legal/analytical status of the surface geometry itself. A vocabulary-referencing value (e.g. `geometry-legal-status:obs`).
Reference to the surface's geometry, e.g. a surface feature collection identifier.
Whether the surface is bounded by (contains) the feature's 2D footprint.
Whether derived geometry has been generated, e.g. `notGenerated` or `solidGenerated`.
The type of derived geometry produced, e.g. `Solid`.
Reference to the generated solid geometry.
Reference to the 2D footprint used as an input to the derivation.
References to the `verticalBoundaryDefinitions` entries used as inputs to the derivation.
References to the `referenceSurfaces` entries used as inputs to the derivation.
Identifier(s) of the supporting source document(s) for the derivation.
Identifier of the PROV activity that generated this derived geometry.
The specific kind of jurisdictional rule applied, e.g. `crownGrantDepthLimit`.
The type of authority or instrument the rule derives from, e.g. `CrownGrant` or `CrownGrantCondition`.
The verbatim source wording the boundary rule was extracted from, e.g. "LIMITED IN DEPTH TO 12.19 METRES BELOW GROUND".
Solid features whose shells reference faces via directed_references. geometry is null.
Ordered list of oriented Shell references bounding the solid. The first entry is the outer boundary Shell; any additional entries describe interior void Shells.
Shell features referencing faces via directed_references. geometry is null.
Ordered list of oriented Face references forming the closed shell surface
Face features whose boundary rings reference edges via directed_references. geometry is null.
Ring features whose boundary segments reference edges via directed_references. geometry is null.
Ordered list of oriented Edge references forming the closed ring boundary
Point features providing base coordinate geometry for the topology
Optional dataset metadata (units, coordinate precision, source info, etc.)
Orientation of the reference: '+' for forward/positive direction, '-' for reverse/negative direction
Identifier of the referenced topological object (e.g. a uuid: URI or local id)
Null when geometry is fully defined by topology references; a GeoJSON geometry object otherwise
